drafted_from: tools/check-how-an-installed-app-is-hardened/tool-rows.json (its sample run), read-data/app-hardening.mjs, read-data/app-hardening.json and test/app-hardening.test.mjs; the sample bundle was run here on 2026-11-13
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check how the app at /Applications/Sample.app is hardened, without launching it, and tell me what falls short." It runs tool:check-an-app on the folder you granted for reading.
no_lists_because: It reads one app bundle and the system's codesign output and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Grant the folder that holds the app (for example /Applications) for reading.
2. Say "Check how /Applications/Sample.app is hardened" and give app as the full path of the bundle inside that folder.

3. Read what comes back: ok is true only when findings is empty; each finding has a kind (no_app, unsigned, not_hardened, entitlement, no_sentinel, unknown_version, fuse, integrity_not_enforced) and its words in said.
4. For a fuse or entitlement finding, tell the app's maker or rebuild the app with that fuse set as the finding's said line asks; a thing that could not be read is a finding, never a pass.

worked_examples.title: An app bundle with only an Info.plist is reported unsigned
worked_examples.given: Observed on 2026-11-13: the sample run of tools/check-an-app's own row (a bundle holding only Contents/Info.plist with CFBundleName Sample) run through run-an-export.mjs and the audit function in tools/check-how-an-installed-app-is-hardened/read-data/app-hardening.mjs, with the real /usr/bin/codesign. codesign reports no signature, so the check stops at that finding; there is no Electron framework to read fuses from.
